name: Encinitas
seo_title: Christmas Events for Kids in Encinitas, CA 2026
seo_desc: Kids' Christmas in Encinitas, CA: the Heritage Tree lighting at Moonlight Beach, Surfing Santa in Cardiff, a holiday parade on 101 and Lightscape.
lede: Encinitas celebrates Christmas beach town style: a giant Norfolk Island pine lit above Moonlight Beach, a Surfing Santa in Cardiff, a parade down Coast Highway 101 and glowing gardens at San Diego Botanic Garden.
celebrates: The season opens downtown with the Encinitas Holiday Street Fair on Coast Highway 101 and San Diego Botanic Garden's Lightscape trail. In early December the Encinitas Chamber of Commerce sets up a free Holiday Village in the Moonlight Beach upper parking lot, and the Encinitas Historical Society lights the city's Heritage Tree, a towering Norfolk Island pine. The next evening the city's Holiday Parade rolls down Coast Highway 101 from D Street to J Street. In Cardiff, Cardiff 101 Main Street hosts the Kringle Mingle with Surfing Santa, and the North Coast Symphony Orchestra plays a family holiday concert with a youth choir.
lastyear: In 2025 the Encinitas Historical Society held the 31st Heritage Tree Lighting on Friday, December 5, beside the Norfolk Island pine at Fourth and C streets. About 500 people came out for the evening. Four children's choirs sang holiday songs, and the band Free Verse played. The Historical Society has run the lighting since 2015, carrying on a tradition that Luis Ortiz started in 1994.
facts: Encinitas means little oaks in Spanish, a name that goes back to Rancho Las Encinitas, granted in 1842. Today's city was formed in 1986, when voters joined Old Encinitas, New Encinitas, Leucadia, Cardiff by the Sea and Olivenhain. Its Christmas tree is a living one: brothers Peter and John Danforth planted a 3 foot Norfolk Island pine in 1952, and it now stands more than 90 feet tall. In 2011 it became one of only two designated Heritage Trees in Encinitas.
trains: The NCTD COASTER stops at Encinitas station, 25 East D Street, in the middle of downtown, just a couple of blocks from Moonlight Beach and right on the Holiday Parade route along Coast Highway 101. The Amtrak Pacific Surfliner stops at Solana Beach to the south and Oceanside to the north, where riders can also catch the SPRINTER inland to Escondido. For a bigger train day, ride a 1907 Baldwin steam locomotive at the Poway-Midland Railroad or see the model layouts at the San Diego Model Railroad Museum in Balboa Park.
train_links: A 1907 Baldwin steam locomotive, a 1906 cable car and a speeder take turns on a narrow gauge loop in Old Poway Park.
Four model railroad clubs fill 27,000 square feet in Balboa Park, and the Toy Train Gallery has a push button layout for kids.
traditions: Since 1994 Encinitas has lit its 1952 Norfolk Island pine at Fourth and C streets, now hosted by the Encinitas Historical Society.
The Encinitas Chamber of Commerce fills the Moonlight Beach upper lot with artisan booths, gingerbread house decorating and hot chocolate on tree lighting day.
Floats, marching bands and costumes roll down Coast Highway 101 between D Street and J Street on an early December evening.
Cardiff 101 Main Street brings Surfing Santa to Aberdeen Drive, where he poses in a vintage Camera Camper sleigh.
Lightscape at San Diego Botanic Garden
The garden turns into an illuminated trail for the holiday season.
kidfact: The Encinitas Christmas tree is alive. It was planted in 1952 when it was only 3 feet tall, and now it is taller than 90 feet.
faq: Where is the Encinitas Heritage Tree?

The Heritage Tree is a Norfolk Island pine at Fourth and C streets in downtown Encinitas, just above Moonlight Beach. Peter and John Danforth planted it in 1952 as a 3 foot sapling, and it now stands more than 90 feet tall. The city named it a Heritage Tree in 2011, and it is lit each December.
Who runs the Encinitas tree lighting?

The Encinitas Historical Society has hosted the Heritage Tree Lighting since 2015, working with the City of Encinitas. The tradition began in 1994 with Luis Ortiz. On the same day, the Encinitas Chamber of Commerce runs a Holiday Village with artisan booths and children's activities in the Moonlight Beach upper parking lot.
Where can kids see Surfing Santa?

At the Cardiff Kringle Mingle on Aberdeen Drive in Cardiff by the Sea, hosted by Cardiff 101 Main Street. Surfing Santa poses for photos in a vintage Camera Camper dressed up as his sleigh, and the morning also has a craft table, live music, a makers market and hot cocoa.
Can we take the train to Christmas events in Encinitas?

Yes. The NCTD COASTER stops at Encinitas station on D Street, a short walk from Moonlight Beach, the Heritage Tree and the Holiday Parade route on Coast Highway 101. Amtrak Pacific Surfliner riders can switch to the COASTER at Solana Beach or Oceanside.

intro_html:
Rally the corgi has sniffed out the best Christmas events for kids in Encinitas for 2026, and here is what he found: 6 family events in Encinitas, 3 of them free. The magic runs from November 20 through January 3 (Lightscape), with Annual Christmas Fest at Seacoast Community Church (December 2), Heritage Tree Lighting and Holiday Village at Moonlight Beach (December 4) and Encinitas Holiday Parade on Highway 101 (December 5) along the way. We check every date on the host’s own website, and each listing links straight there. For the rest of the state, see our California Christmas events for kids guide.
